column1: # The PC port's own menu strings, and the one place they are written.
# Bloodborne's option screens own one thousand-id block each: 110000 System,
# 111000 Environment, 112000 Brightness, 113000 Controls, 114000 Network,
# 115000 Language. Inside a block, N is a row and N+20 is the screen title -
# 110000..110005 are the System list's rows and 110020 is the word "System".
# The port takes the next free blocks - 116000 PC Settings, 117000 PC
# Graphics, 118000 PC Controls, 119000 Key Bindings, 120000 PC Effects, 121000
# PC Camera, 122000 the title menu's Quit Game, 123000 Steam Deck (shown on a
# Deck only), 124000 PC Enhancements, 125000 PC Upscaling - and 110006..110014 for the System rows
# that open them. All are unused in the shipped menu.msgbnd. (Motion blur,
# depth of field and chromatic aberration moved to PC Effects with their
# bbhost builds this file in and writes these into menu.msgbnd.dcx at start
# (src/engine/menu_assets.cpp); the ids
# are what src/engine/option_menu.cpp asks the message repository for, so the
# text lives here and nowhere else.
# Ids 920000..929999 are dialog text instead (group 78, the generic yes/no
# dialog's - engine/live_resolution.cpp opens one); the help column is unused.
# Ids 14000332..14000399 are event text (group 30): the talk menus' entries and
# the messages their scripts show - the Altar of Despair's rebirth
# (engine/rebirth_script.h); the help column is unused.
# A "\n" in the text is a line break.
# The line help is one line under the rows, cut off where it runs past the
# dialog (about 130 characters of its font): keep a row's help to 96
# characters, which tests/menu_assets_test.cpp checks.
# id

column3: A frame made between each two of the game's. The game runs at half your refresh rate, or less.
Sharpens the 3D after TAA, FSR or DLSS; 0 leaves it as it is. Needs Upscaling on.
Reflection resolution: Quarter is about four times cheaper; Half is the game's own, sharper.
Replaces the game's AA: TAA or FSR 3 (any GPU), FSR 4 (AMD, Windows only) or DLSS (NVIDIA RTX).
The 3D's drawn size: Performance half, Balanced 59%, Quality two thirds, Native AA full size.
How much TAA smooths: higher is steadier but may leave a faint trail, lower crisper. Default 5.
Precise (default): clean edges, about 1% at 4K. Off: a bit faster, softer edges, a faint trail.
